title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is abuzz with IPO ambitions, nuclear propulsion developments, and the ongoing push for space computing. Meanwhile, military applications of space technology continue to attract significant investment and attention.

themes.title: IPO Fever in Space
themes.body: SpaceX's potential $75 billion IPO is drawing eyes, while other firms like Applied Aerospace & Defense are also looking to capitalize on the market. This could signal a broader trend of financial optimism in the sector, albeit with a side of skepticism about the sustainability of such valuations.

themes.title: Nuclear Propulsion Progress
themes.body: NASA's efforts to streamline nuclear electric propulsion development are gaining momentum, promising a new era of deep space exploration. As the agency pushes forward, it raises questions about the balance between innovation and safety in the nuclear realm.

themes.title: Space Computing Initiatives
themes.body: China's institutional framework for space computing is a clear signal of its ambitions in this critical area, which could reshape global competition. As nations race to establish dominance, the implications for data processing and satellite operations are significant.

themes.title: Military Space Investments
themes.body: With a $1.4 billion boost to the space resilience budget and Anduril teaming with L3Harris for tactical SDA constellations, military interest in space tech is intensifying. This trend reflects a growing recognition of space as a critical domain for national security.
